summary: This memo gives an IAB recommendation for CIDR as a short-term strategy to stretch the life of the 32-bit IP address space and slow the growth of routing tables. It is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo recommends CIDR as a way to use the existing IP address space more efficiently and slow routing-table growth. It presents CIDR as an interim strategy while a longer-term solution is developed.

questions: why did the iab recommend cidr
how does cidr address routing-table growth
subtitle: Endorses CIDR as an interim way to conserve IPv4 addresses and limit routing-table growth.

tldr.problem: The Internet's 32-bit IP address space and the routing tables in transit routers were both under pressure from rapid growth.
tldr.mechanism: CIDR combines managed address allocation with route aggregation so that address blocks can be allocated efficiently and routing information can be summarized.
tldr.outcome: The IAB endorses CIDR as an immediate-term strategy while the technical community works on a longer-term solution. Unit metadata classifies this RFC as Historic.

today: RFC 1481 is classified as Historic in the unit metadata. It records the IAB's recommendation to use CIDR as an intermediate strategy for address and routing-table scaling.

sections.title: The Scaling Problem
sections.content:
The memo says Internet growth was putting pressure on two parts of the network. The existing 32-bit IP address space needed to be conserved, and routing tables in transit routers were growing rapidly.

Allocating blocks of Class C numbers could also increase routing-table entries unless routing protocols aggregated related routes.
sections.plainLanguage: The Internet needed to conserve addresses and control the number of routes that routers had to store. Address allocation and routing summaries needed to work together.

sections.title: CIDR as an Interim Strategy
sections.content:
Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) combines management of IP address allocation with a way to aggregate routing information. The memo describes these as the two basic components of the plan.

It frames CIDR as an immediate-term strategy for extending the life of the existing 32-bit address space, while assuming that the technical community is addressing a longer-term solution.
sections.plainLanguage: CIDR changes how address blocks are assigned and how routers combine route information. The memo presents it as a way to buy time, not as the long-term solution itself.

sections.title: IAB Endorsement
sections.content:
The IAB endorses the CIDR architecture and its implementation. It also supports the actions of IANA, InterNIC, router vendors, and network operators to put CIDR into practice.

The memo is informational and does not specify an Internet standard.
sections.plainLanguage: The IAB supports CIDR and the work to implement it. This memo is a recommendation, not a protocol specification.

references.text: Fuller, V., Li, T., Yu, J., and K. Varadhan, "Supernetting: an Address Assignment and Aggregation Strategy", RFC 1338, June 1992.
Gerich, E., "Guidelines for management of IP Address Space", RFC 1466, May 1993.
